2. **Put the decision-critical specifics immediately beside the price/CTA.**  
   The page does eventually specify the kit contents—8m edge protection, 12 corner guards, 12 socket protectors (10 5A/2 15A), 10 cabinet locks, 2 fridge locks, and 4 door guards—but this useful scope appears lower down. ([thepeachbucket.com](https://thepeachbucket.com/products/the-peach-bucket-6-in-1-child-safety-kit))

3. **Make the “whole-home” promise more precise.**  
   “Childproof your entire home” and “complete child safety system” are broad relative to a six-zone kit. Public safety guidance identifies additional hazard controls, including keeping dangerous substances secured, outlet protection, cords, furniture-related risks, and gates where relevant. The kit can credibly be positioned as a starter/common-hazards system, but the page should plainly list important exclusions rather than imply a universally complete solution. ([thepeachbucket.com](https://thepeachbucket.com/products/the-peach-bucket-6-in-1-child-safety-kit))  
   This is not a criticism of the kit; it is a trust-risk reduction: parents who spot an obvious missing category may question the rest of the claims.

4. **Substantiate or narrowly define trust-heavy claims.**  
   The page makes several high-impact claims: “food grade & BPA free,” “every single piece manually human tested,” Made in India, ₹20 lakh+ contributed, 30-day money-back guarantee, 720-day replacement guarantee, and free 1:1 support. These may all be true, but the product page currently provides little public evidence or operational detail next to them. ([thepeachbucket.com](https://thepeachbucket.com/products/the-peach-bucket-6-in-1-child-safety-kit))  
   Prioritize proof rather than more promises:
   - exact warranty eligibility, claim process, and exclusions;
   - return conditions and refund timeline;
   - what “human tested” means;
   - material/test documentation if held;
   - how and when video support is booked;
   - evidence for the giving claim, if it is to remain a purchase driver.  
   Do **not** add certifications, safety-test results, or endorsements unless the business can document them.

5. **Address the “kit vs. only what I need” objection.**  
   Parent discussions are anecdotal—not representative market research—but Indian comments identify socket covers, cupboard locks and edge protection as core needs; a recent India-focused thread also reports variable usefulness by item and household. Other parent discussions argue for babyproofing incrementally rather than buying a universal list. ([reddit.com](https://www.reddit.com/r/Frugal_Ind/comments/1hqvqh4/how_to_baby_proof_home/?utm_source=openai))  
   The page already links to “Build Your Own Childproofing Kit,” but the product page should make the choice easy: a short home/child-stage selector, or visibly framed options for “start with essentials” versus “six-zone setup.” This is a hypothesis to test, **not** evidence that the ₹3,299 bundle is incorrectly priced.

### Messaging / audience observations

- “For the Top 1% of Indian Parents” is a conspicuous homepage positioning choice. It may create premium aspiration, but it may also signal exclusion or make a practical safety product feel status-coded. Test a version without this line; do not assume it is the cause of non-purchase. ([thepeachbucket.com](https://thepeachbucket.com/))
- The strongest credible page differentiators are convenience and India-specific fit: tool-free/no-drill setup, stated 5A/15A socket allocation, extra adhesive, and live setup support. These are more concrete than broad “peace of mind” language and should be visually demonstrated close to purchase. ([thepeachbucket.com](https://thepeachbucket.com/products/the-peach-bucket-6-in-1-child-safety-kit))
- Public guidance supports the general safety relevance of cabinet locks and outlet covers, but it does **not** validate Peach Bucket’s particular products, installation, or effectiveness. ([cpsc.gov](https://www.cpsc.gov/safety-education/safety-guides/kids-and-babies/Childproofing-Your-Home?utm_source=openai))

### Suggested validation sequence
1. Audit live stock/CTA/delivery/scarcity consistency on mobile and desktop.  
2. Test a high-page “contents + fit + exclusions + returns/warranty” block.  
3. Test removing “Top 1%” and emphasizing concrete fit/support.  
4. Test bundle framing versus an obvious build-your-own route.  
5. Collect actual buyer/non-buyer objections before changing price, offers, or guarantee terms.

### Exact access gaps / uncertainties
- Could not access sales funnel, conversion rate, abandonment, inventory system, checkout/payment methods, delivery coverage, customer-support response time, returns, customer reviews, or ad-message alignment.
- The crawl showed image placeholders but did not permit a reliable visual/mobile UX assessment.
- The linked Return Policy could not be reviewed within available public access; therefore, the exact money-back conditions are unknown.
- Reddit evidence is limited anecdote; most cited discussion is not India-specific. Only the India-oriented threads should be treated as locally relevant, and even those do not establish prevalence."}

{
  "answer_markdown": "## The diagnosis: it is not only a product-page problem

Your store recorded **4,452 sessions → 112 add-to-carts (2.5%) → 101 checkouts (2.3%) → 34 completed checkouts (0.76%)**.

That says two things:

1. **The product page needs more purchase confidence** — most visitors do not add to cart.
2. **Checkout completion is the biggest leak** — only **34% of reached checkouts** became completed checkouts. A better product page alone will not recover those lost orders.

Do **not** cut price yet. At ₹3,299, the kit has a meaningful bundle decision to justify, but your current data does not prove price is the objection. Fix clarity, trust and checkout friction first.

---

## Change these on the product page first

### 1. Fix stock, delivery and CTA contradictions immediately
Your public homepage was observed showing both **“Out of stock”** and **“Only 48 kits left. Delivery in 2–7 days.”** This can kill a purchase even if checkout technically works.

**One source of truth required:**
- If available: `In stock • Dispatch/delivery estimate shown at checkout` (only if true)
- If unavailable: remove purchase CTA and use `Notify me when back in stock`
- Remove “only X left” unless it is inventory-linked and accurate.

Also test every product variant and CTA on mobile: Add to Cart, Buy Now, cart drawer and checkout.

### 2. Replace the broad hero promise with a concrete buying decision
“Childproof your entire home” sounds bigger than a six-category kit and can trigger scepticism. Lead with what parents receive, where it works, and how setup happens.

**Recommended above-the-fold copy:**

> ### Start childproofing the everyday danger zones at home
> One India-ready kit for sharp furniture edges, sockets, cabinets, fridge access and doors — with a guided, tool-free setup.
>
> **Inside this kit:** 8m edge protection • 12 corner guards • 12 socket protectors (10 × 5A, 2 × 15A) • 10 cabinet locks • 2 fridge locks • 4 door guards
>
> **Designed for:** common Indian modular switchboards, wooden furniture/doors, modular kitchens and refrigerators.
>
> **Before you buy:** This is a starter kit for six common home danger zones. It does not replace adult supervision or cover every home-safety need such as gates, furniture anchoring or securing hazardous substances.
>
> **[Add the 6-in-1 Kit — ₹3,299]**
> *Need only a few items? Build your own kit →*

This makes the ₹3,299 feel like a defined solution rather than an expensive assortment of unknown parts.

### 3. Add a “Will it work in my home?” block directly below the CTA
This is likely the practical hesitation for an Indian-home product: socket type, adhesive, furniture finish, cabinets and installation difficulty.

**Section title:** `Check fit before you order`

| Area | What the kit is intended for | Confirm before buying |
|---|---|---|
| Sockets | Common modular 5A / 15A switchboards | Compare your socket layout to the product photos |
| Furniture edges | Everyday tables, beds and sharp furniture edges | Check the surface is clean, dry and suitable for adhesive |
| Cabinets & fridge | Wooden/modular cabinets and refrigerators | Check handle/door configuration against installation guide |
| Doors | Common interior doors | Check door gap and closing style |

Add real close-up photos/video for each installation—not generic family/lifestyle imagery. Include the actual surface, the adhesive application, and the item after installation.

### 4. Make support and guarantee operational, not vague
The site currently claims 1:1 video support, a 30-day money-back guarantee and a 720-day eligible-failure replacement guarantee. These are strong conversion assets **only when buyers can understand them in 10 seconds**.

Place an accordion beside/below Add to Cart:

- **Need setup help?** “After ordering, contact us on [channel] to book/get 1:1 installation video guidance.”
- **30-day returns:** state eligibility, condition required, return shipping responsibility and refund timing.
- **720-day replacement:** define “eligible failure,” what is excluded, and how to make a claim.

Only use this wording once operations can honour it exactly. Do not add unsupported safety certifications or claims such as “prevents injuries.”

### 5. Turn the bundle objection into a choice, not a dead end
Some parents will think: “I only need socket covers and cabinet locks.” Make that objection visible and harmless.

**Add this comparison near the first CTA:**

| Choose the 6-in-1 kit if… | Build your own kit if… |
|---|---|
| Your baby is crawling/exploring and you want to cover several common zones now | You need protection for one or two specific areas |
| You prefer one guided setup | You already know exactly what your home needs |

**CTA pair:**
- `Get the 6-in-1 Home Starter Kit`
- `Shop individual safety essentials`

This may reduce some bundle sales, but it is better than losing high-intent visitors entirely—and lets you learn whether bundle scope is the objection.
